## Download

Download **`Rastro-windows-x64.exe`** below and run it. There's nothing to install. Windows will probably warn you the first time because the file isn't signed yet: click **More info → Run anyway**. The [README](https://github.com/MaxSala/rastro-tarkov#is-it-safe) explains why, and how to check the file yourself.

Already using Rastro? Close it and replace the old `.exe` with this one. Your settings, points, maps and prices are kept.

## What's new

**Quests, built around your raid**
- A new **Quests** section (`Ctrl+4`) with every quest from tarkov.dev, in your language. It shows what you're on, what you can start next and, for everything else, exactly what's missing: your level or the quests that come first.
- Set your level and faction once. Filter by trader, map or Kappa, and search quests, objectives and the items they ask for.
- Every quest shows its trader, the quest's picture and **what it gives you**: experience, reputation, items, and the trader offers and crafts it unlocks.
- Starting mid-wipe? Open the quest you're on and press **Mark the previous quests as done**: your progress is up to date in one click.

**On the map, only what matters now**
- The open objectives of your active quests appear on the map as amber markers, with a symbol for what to do there: go, mark, plant, find, shoot or extract. Areas show their real outline on the ground. Hover one to see what to do; click it and Rastro guides you there with distance, direction and height, the same way it does for extracts. Floors work too.
- The new **Quests** panel (`5`) lists what you can do on the map you're on, nearest first. Tick objectives off, or count kills with − and +, without leaving the map.
- **Show on map** previews any quest on its map before you take it.

**Don't sell what you'll need**
- The Market now tells you which of your quests still ask for an item, how many you need and whether it has to be found in raid.

**Your language, everywhere**
- Change the language and Rastro offers to bring your maps, prices and quests over to it. Tick *Always* (or turn it on in *Settings → General*) and it does it by itself. Maps aren't downloaded again: only their names and texts.

**Private and offline**
- Your quest progress stays on your PC, separately for PvP and PvE. Rastro only connects to tarkov.dev when you download or refresh the quests, and to fetch the pictures you open.

**Fixes**
- Running a command from the command palette that opens a dialog, such as *What's new*, no longer closes it straight away.
- Quest spots that fall outside the map (bad data) are no longer drawn.

Full history in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/MaxSala/rastro-tarkov/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
